topic: Projectile Motion: Initial Velocity, Height, Air Resistance, Mass
key_concepts: Projectile motion follows a curved path whose range and height can be measured.
Increasing initial launch speed increases the projectile's maximum height and range.
Increasing initial launch speed increases time to maximum height and total flight time.
Increasing launch height increases the projectile's range and total flight time.
Air resistance changes the projectile's path compared with ideal no-air-resistance motion.
Air resistance reduces the projectile's maximum height and range.
The effect of air resistance on projectile motion varies with altitude.
Mass influences a projectile's motion path when air resistance is present.
Projectile motion can be investigated using simulations and physical catapult models.
At a fixed launch angle, initial speed, height, air resistance, and mass affect trajectory
